title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site OPS, and Top Support Issues
author: Evelyn Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This page defines the standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation focused on SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site publishing, and the canonical set of top support issues and fixes. The goal is a consistent, low-friction onboarding experience for engineers and product teams using Redwood Inference SDKs and APIs.

Scope
-----
Applies to: devex docs authors, SDK maintainers, devrel, solutions engineering, and support engineers.
Includes: JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, cURL examples, quickstart templates, docs-site publishing procedures, and the canonical top support issues with step-by-step fixes.
Excludes: internal design notes, research experiments, and personal tickets.

Owner & Contacts
-----------------
- Doc owner: Developer Experience (Docs) \u2014 Evelyn Chen
- Primary contacts: Miguel Torres (SDK lead), Aisha Patel (DevRel), Sanjay Rao (Support Escalations)
- Slack channels: #devex-docs, #sdk-issues, #support-canonical-fixes

Audience
--------
- Internal: SDK engineers, support, solutions engineering, product
- External (secondary): early-adopter customers, integration partners (examples are public-safe; sensitive internal runbooks live elsewhere)

Standards & Conventions
-----------------------
All DevEx docs MUST follow these conventions:
- Structure: short intro, prerequisites, step-by-step quickstart, code examples, troubleshooting, and links to related pages.
- Tone: prescriptive, example-driven, and platform-focused. Use full sentences.
- Formatting: use H2/H3 headings, numbered steps for procedures, bullet lists for options, and monospaced font for inline code.
- Samples: provide at least one minimal working example and one production-ready snippet illustrating best practices (error handling, retries, idempotency).
- Snippets: keep examples copy-paste runnable. If using API keys or environment variables, show secure best practice patterns (e.g. use environment vars, not hard-coded keys).

Templates (Quickstarts & SDK Guides)
-----------------------------------
We provide canonical templates to speed authoring. Use these templates and replace placeholders.
1) Quickstart template (single-page)
   - Title 
   - Short summary (1\u20132 sentences)
   - Prerequisites (account, CLI, API key, Python/Node versions)
   - 5\u20138 minute quickstart steps (install, auth, first request, verify)
   - Next steps (links to SDK reference, advanced examples)

2) SDK Guide template (multi-page)
   - Overview and key concepts (models, routing, streaming)
   - Installation and versioning guidance
   - Core API surface (auth, client creation, common patterns)
   - Error model and retry patterns
   - Examples (minimal, streaming, function/tool calling, embeddings)
   - Migration notes for breaking changes

3) API Examples (per-endpoint)
   - Endpoint summary + expected inputs/outputs
   - Minimal curl + Python + Node examples (see canonical examples below)
   - Response schema examples and common error codes

Canonical Examples (copy-paste safe)
------------------------------------
- JavaScript (Node) minimal generation example:
  ```js
  // Install: npm install @redwood-inference/sdk
  const { Redwood } = require('@redwood-inference/sdk')
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
  async function main() {
    const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1.0', prompt: 'Write a short haiku about latency.' })
    console.log(res.text)
  }
  main().catch(console.error)
  ```

- Python minimal embeddings example:
  ```py
  # pip install redwood-inference
  import os
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
  vectors = c.embeddings.create(model='embed-small', input=['redwood inference', 'low latency'])
  print(vectors[0]['embedding'][:8])
  ```

- cURL example (simple chat call):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1.0","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize Redwood Inference in one sentence."}]}'

Docs Site Operating Procedures (Publishing Flow)
------------------------------------------------
Purpose: ensure docs are accurate, discoverable, and safe to publish.
1) Drafting
   - Create page using the Quickstart or SDK Guide template. Include required metadata (owner, reviewers, tags).
2) Review
   - Peer review by at least one SDK engineer and one DevRel reviewer. Use the reviewers field.
   - Run code samples in the canonical examples CI job (see docs-site pipeline).
3) Accessibility & SEO
   - Add descriptive title, short summary, and 1\u20132 sentence meta description in page metadata.
4) Merge & Deploy
   - Merge to docs repo branch and ensure the docs CI checks pass (lint, example-runner, link-checker).
   - Release to staging site; manual smoke test of examples.
   - Promote to production site; tag the page with release date.
5) Post-publish
   - Announce in #devex-docs and optionally in release notes.

Publishing Checklist (required)
- [ ] Title and owner populated
- [ ] Reviewers listed and sign-off recorded
- [ ] All code snippets execute in CI
- [ ] Links and images validated by link-checker
- [ ] Labels (tags) added: language, topic, product-area
- [ ] Related pages set

Versioning and Deprecation Policy
----------------------------------
- Docs tied to SDK major versions (v1, v2): pages should state supported SDK versions at top.
- When deprecating endpoints or SDK features: create a migration guide, add "deprecated" banner, and schedule removal aligned with SDK EOL calendar (90-day minimum warning for customers).

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (canonical-fixes)
-----------------------------------------------------
This section lists the top recurring support issues we include in quickstarts and SDK guides as preemptive troubleshooting. Each entry contains: symptom, root cause(s), quick triage commands, canonical fix, and KB link.
1) Authentication errors (401/403)
   - Symptom: API returns 401 or 403 immediately
   - Root causes: missing/rotated API key, wrong environment variable name, scope mismatch
   - Triage: curl -I with Authorization header; check env: echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY
   - Canonical fix: confirm key in Secrets Manager, rotate if compromised, update env var names in README example
   - KB: /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/authn-troubleshooting

2) Slow first-token latency for workloads on cold endpoints
   - Symptom: first token takes 800\u20132000ms while subsequent tokens are fast
   - Root cause: model cold start, missing prefix caching, or oversized batch config
   - Fix: enable warmup policy in route config, use streaming, or configure short-lived pre-warm requests in dedicated pools
   - KB: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/initial-latency-mitigation

3) Streaming not returning partial tokens
   - Symptom: client receives buffered response until completion
   - Root cause: incorrect use of SDK stream API or missing SSE/ws handling in client
   - Fix: follow streaming example in SDK guide (attach event handlers, use text/event-stream)
   - KB: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/streaming-api-examples

4) Embeddings mismatch across SDK versions
   - Symptom: Similarity scores differ after SDK upgrade
   - Root cause: model variant change or normalization differences in SDK
   - Fix: pin model and SDK major version in quickstart; include reproducibility notes and test vectors

5) High 429 rate-limited errors in burst traffic
   - Symptom: 429s during short load spikes
   - Root cause: missing client-side retry/backoff or insufficient burst capacity in Dedicated
   - Fix: implement exponential backoff with jitter (example below) and request burst capacity increase for Dedicated customers
   - Example retry snippet (JS):
     ```js
     async function withRetry(fn, retries=5) {
       for (let i=0;i<retries;i++) {
         try { return await fn() }
         catch(e) {
           if (!isRetryable(e) || i===retries-1) throw e
           await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, Math.pow(2,i)*100 + Math.random()*100))
         }
       }
     }
     ```

6) Mismatched content type errors (400)
   - Symptom: API returns 400 with message about invalid JSON or content-type
   - Fix: ensure Content-Type: application/json and valid JSON body; include example curl check.

7) Persistent KV cache inconsistencies in streaming sessions
   - Symptom: incorrect continuations when resuming sessions
   - Root cause: client restoring incorrect KV cache or model mismatch
   - Fix: include canonical session restore example and KV cache checksum verification in SDK docs

8) Unexpected tokenization differences across locales
   - Symptom: token counts differ for same input on different hosts
   - Fix: document tokenizer version, ensure consistent normalization (NFKC), and pin tokenizer version in SDK

9) OOM errors during large-batch inference
   - Symptom: worker crashes with OOM on large batch requests
   - Fix: recommend batch-size ceiling table (see table), enable progressive batching, or use a higher-memory instance profile

Batch size guidance table:
Model family | Recommended max batch size | Notes
redwood-1.x   | 8                        | For 16GB GPU; reduce for long context lengths
redwood-small | 64                       | CPU/quantized runs ok
chat-optimized | 4                       | Streaming-enabled recommended

10) Incorrect function/tool calling behavior
   - Symptom: model ignores tool schema or formats response incorrectly
   - Fix: ensure function schema follows JSON Schema subset we expect, include example tool-calling payloads, and add schema validation in SDK wrappers

Triaging & Escalation Process
-----------------------------
- Support engineers should attempt canonical fixes first (listed above). If unresolved escalate to #support-canonical-fixes with: error logs, request IDs, region, model, SDK version, and minimal repro.
- For potential product regressions tag issue as "regression" and notify eng-servicing-runtime on-call.

Metrics & Reporting
-------------------
Track these metrics to measure doc effectiveness:
- Page views and time-on-page for quickstarts
- Number of support tickets referencing canonical-fixes KB entries
- CI sample-run pass rate (code examples running in CI)
- Time-to-first-success for new customers (measured via onboarding funnels)

Maintenance Schedule
--------------------
- Quarterly review of quickstarts and SDK guides (owners get reminder in docs workflow)
- Immediate update required after SDK major releases or breaking API changes
- Archive old examples and mark with deprecation banner if SDK EOL > 90 days

Appendix: Useful Commands & CI Jobs
----------------------------------
- docs-site lint: yarn docs:lint
- example-runner CI job: .github/workflows/examples.yml (runs Node and Python snippets)
- link checker: yarn docs:link-check
- publish: yarn docs:deploy --staging then --prod

Related Pages
-------------

- SDK reference pages per language
- Eng-serving-runtime performance guides

Questions or feedback? Open a PR against the docs repo and tag @evelyn.chen for review.
